text:
john_customer: Hey, our integration started getting 502/504s to the Redwood inference API around 09:23 UTC. Error looks like a gateway TLS handshake timeout. Anyone else seeing this?
alex: can you paste the full curl? are you hitting api.redwood.com or a private endpoint?
john_customer: hitting api.redwood.com/v1/generate. curl returns "(56) TLS handshake" and the response is a 502 from our client proxy. reproduced from two regions.
jamie: thx. we're not aware of a deploy at that time. @maria can you check edge logs and resolver metrics?
maria: looking now, pulling edge LB logs for the last 30m. seeing several TLS handshake timeouts from a subset of IPs. Also seeing spikes in resolver timeouts for one resolver pool (10.8.3.0/24).
kaito: curious — any cert rotation recently? OCSP stapling is enabled; if stapling fails the backend can still handshake, but some clients reject missing stapled response.
alex: no cert rollout in org, last rotation was last week. but we did push a change to edge LB routing policy ~2h ago.
maria: grep logs: `edge-lb[conn]: handshake_timeout client=203.0.113.24 server=edge-19` repeated 42x. Also `ocsp: staple fetch error: upstream timeout` from edge-19.
jamie: ahh, OCSP fetch errors. maybe our OCSP responder or egress path had issues.
john_customer: is that why they see 502s? they see "upstream handshake timeout".
alex: yes possible — if edge can't fetch OCSP staple and the client enforces stapled response, some handshakes will fail. But we usually allow handshakes without stapling if not strict.
maria: adding more: DNS traces show resolver returns stale A record pointing to decommissioned edge-19 for some clients due to cached negative TTLs. combination of stale DNS and ocsp fail -> handshake to wrong/misconfigured backend.
kaito: can you paste `dig +short api.redwood.com @8.8.8.8` and `@<customer resolver>` results? we need repro.
john_customer: `@8.8.8.8` -> 198.51.100.45; `@their-resolver` -> 198.51.100.45 as well. But tracepath shows their traffic hitting 198.51.100.219 in some probes.
alex: 219 is retired host from last month. that explains mismatched cert (SNI mismatch) causing handshake aborts.
jamie: action: rotate DNS to purge stale entry and force short TTL propagation. Also trigger edge host decommission cleanup to remove stale IPs from LB pools.
maria: I'm reloading OCSP stapling worker and forcing a re-fetch: `systemctl restart ocsp-fetcher && ocspctl fetch --all`. can someone validate traffic after restart?
john_customer: testing now — looks better for me, no TLS errors in the last 1 minute. 200 responses again. :tada:
alex: sweet. still want to keep monitoring. setting a short-term mitigation: 60s DNS TTL for api.redwood.com and remove old IPs from the pool.
kaito: follow-ups: 1) investigate why OCSP fetcher timed out (egress routing/ratelimit), 2) ensure decommissioned hosts are fully evicted from DNS/LB inventory, 3) add alert for stale DNS records hitting live traffic.
jamie: filed infra ticket INF-8472 and assigned to @kaito. logged timeline and commands used.
maria: added console incident note and pinned logs to channel. deploying a small probe to validate OCSP staple freshness every 30s across regions.
john_customer: thanks all — we'll keep an eye and ping if it reoccurs.
support-bot: Incident created: #1842101120 - TLS/OCSP responder timeouts + DNS stale IP causing handshake failures. Priority: P2
alex: closing thread after 2h of stable traffic unless anyone objects.
jamie: ok closing, please re-open if anomalies return. :thumbsup:
